title: Deep learning classifies esophageal cancer and precursor lesions in endoscopic images
summary: A no-code deep-learning tool trained on 5162 white-light endoscopic images classified esophageal cancers, dysplasias and non-neoplasms, reaching 95.6% internal-test accuracy. In an external test of 836 new images from five hospitals, which the authors describe as prospective, accuracy ranged from 90.0% to 95.8% (overall 93.9%). Results are image-level and from still images rather than live endoscopy.
ai_technology: No-code deep-learning image classifier with attention-map explainability
organization: Department of Internal Medicine, Gangneung Asan Hospital, University of Ulsan College of Medicine, Gangneung, Korea; Department of Internal Medicine, Hallym University College of Medicine, Chuncheon, Korea

evidence.tested: Internal test plus an external test of 836 images from five hospitals, with accuracy of 90.0-95.8%.
evidence.unknown: Per-patient or real-time clinical performance; the external images were a fixed set evaluated at image level; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A deep learning model classified endoscopic images into cancer, dysplasia and non-neoplasm.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from the review input and author affiliations from Crossref metadata for this DOI. Publisher full text not accessed.
